reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about dislocation behavior, interface sliding, and creep response in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the unique combined effects of severe lattice distortion and short-range order on creep in such systems.
premises: Severe lattice distortion and short-range order at FCC/BCC interfaces create localized stress concentrations that serve as preferential dislocation nucleation sites.
Lattice distortions and short-range order hinder dislocation recovery and transmission, leading to dislocation pile-ups.
Dislocation pile-ups initially pin deformation, causing a lower creep strain rate.
Overwhelmed barriers trigger localized interface sliding, accelerating plastic deformation.
FCC/BCC high-entropy multilayers will show a distinct two-stage creep response (initial lower rate, then acceleration) compared to conventional multilayers or homogeneous alloys.
